features.name: AI answer engines and buyer discovery
features.description: AI-powered answer engines are aggregating content from multiple sources and changing how buyers discover products. Buyers now see AI summaries instead of individual web pages, and marketers need strategies to be visible in these engines.
caveats: This is a current reality marketers are experiencing

features.name: AI agents in buying and evaluation
features.description: AI agents are now evaluating and choosing products alongside humans. Marketers must ensure their content is understandable and persuasive not just to human buyers but also to AI agents making purchasing decisions.
caveats: Agents are actively participating in evaluation but specific use cases not detailed

features.name: AI-powered content repurposing at scale
features.description: Using AI to take core human-produced content and repurpose it across multiple channels and platforms simultaneously. This addresses the need for visibility everywhere without proportional increase in marketing resources.
caveats: No magic bullet; requires strategic execution
Requires original thought or compelling point of view to work effectively
AI alone cannot create differentiated content

features.name: Anonymous buyer research phase shift
features.description: Research studies show buyers now conduct the majority of research anonymously and form a finalist list with 85% accuracy before speaking to sales. This means visibility during the anonymous research phase is critical.
caveats: Based on independent research studies

features.name: Building in public and thought leadership content
features.description: Successful startups gain market share by putting out smart and helpful free content across podcasts, YouTube, LinkedIn, and other channels. This content builds awareness and trust before buyers engage in sales conversations.
caveats: Requires consistent effort and meaningful content quality

features.name: Brand gravity concept for buyer engagement
features.description: Building enough digital mass online to create strong gravitational pull that attracts buyers and keeps them in orbit until ready to make a decision, without forcing them.

features.name: Employee voice amplification strategy
features.description: Marketing leaders should focus resources on amplifying voices of smart and helpful employees who resonate with target audience rather than intensifying corporate page posts.
caveats: Requires care and support for employees to retain them
Works best when employees authentically share their point of view

features.name: LinkedIn-focused content differentiation
features.description: Content on LinkedIn must be compelling, differentiated and valuable with depth that cannot be obtained from asking a question in ChatGPT, with substantial detail and multiple formats like carousels and infographics.
caveats: Generic AI-generated content will appear as slop
Must avoid checklist indicators of AI-only writing
Corporate pages less effective than individual voices

features.name: Corporate versus personal page trust dynamics
features.description: People now trust individual leaders and subject matter experts over corporate pages, preferring human points of view even for company news like acquisitions, mergers or product launches.
caveats: Corporate pages still useful for formal news announcements
Trust transfer requires consistent authenticity from individuals

features.name: AI agents for website research and information retrieval
features.description: AI agents that autonomously research websites and retrieve relevant data points, white papers, and assets without requiring manual intervention or traditional search.
caveats: user is ahead of typical adoption curve
not yet mainstream

features.name: AI chat capabilities for conversational website interaction
features.description: Simple AI chat interfaces added to websites allowing users to ask questions directly without navigating complex page hierarchies, with capabilities to serve both human and AI agent consumers.
caveats: early adoption by forward-thinking marketing leaders
reported significant conversion improvements

features.name: Personal brand amplification through content and visibility programs
features.description: Strategic programs that expose experts and employees through micro-sites, white papers, articles, and speaking engagements to build trust and market share, showing measurable increases in billable hours and profitability.
caveats: requires organizational commitment and willingness to invest in personal brand
initially faced internal resistance from leadership

features.name: AI-native competitive displacement
features.description: AI-native startups gaining market share from traditional organizations by being more agile and leveraging AI capabilities, particularly in product development and market reach.

features.name: AI-powered content generation for marketing
features.description: Using AI to generate marketing assets like infographics from source materials, reducing time and skill requirements while enabling rapid content production at scale.
caveats: shifts effort from creation to instruction
raises questions about human effort and authenticity

features.name: Voice dictation workflows
features.description: Shift from typing to voice-based input for creating content and conducting research, enabled by tools like Whisper. Represents a natural progression in AI adoption.

features.name: AI for lead enrichment
features.description: Using AI to enrich customer records with missing data before sales hand-off. High-impact, low-effort use case that supports pipeline creation and deal acceleration.

features.name: AI-powered campaign production acceleration
features.description: Using AI to accelerate campaign creation and execution. Reduces campaign time-to-market from 92 days to 2 weeks through AI-forward approaches or outsourced partners.
caveats: results can be achieved through outsourcing to AI-forward partners
